_comment: Locked, global, production design system. Every value here applies to every post identically. Nothing in this file is derived from an image, computed automatically, or sampled from a photo — it is fixed by hand and stays fixed. Per-post layout (position, sizes) lives in config/layouts.json.

canvas._note: Each master's own dimensions are preserved exactly. This is only a sanity check that a master is still ~4:5 — never a resize/crop target.

templates._comment: 3 deterministic, reusable 4:5 templates. The canvas is always the MASTER's own width/height (never resized/upscaled) — masters in this project come in a few different native sizes (1122x1402, 928x1152, 1126x1397, ...), so A/C panel geometry is stored as a RATIO of the master's own dimensions, not a fixed pixel size. A post's layout entry sets `template: "A"|"B"|"C"` and, for A/C, `photoCrop` (the region extracted from the master, in the MASTER's own pixel coordinates) — its width/height must exactly equal that master's own computed panel size (canvasWidth*photoPanelWidthRatio for A, canvasHeight*photoBandHeightRatio for C, each rounded) so no scaling is ever needed. Master files are never touched; only this derived, in-memory crop is composited onto a flat cream canvas.

A._description: Editorial split — a solid cream text panel on the left, the photo (cropped to fill) on the right. Text never touches the photo at all.

B._description: Full image — text overlaid directly on the full photo. Only for a photo with genuinely large clean negative space; never forced.

C._description: Photo top / text bottom — the photo (cropped to fill) on top, a solid cream text band below it. Text never touches the photo at all.
